questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: To form a complete monolayer of acetic acid on $1 \mathrm{~g}$ of charcoal, $100 \mathrm{~mL}$ of $0.5 \mathrm{M}$ acetic acid was used. Some of the acetic acid remained unadsorbed. To neutralize the unadsorbed acetic acid, 40 $\mathrm{mL}$ of $1 \mathrm{M} \mathrm{NaOH}$ solution was required. If each molecule of acetic acid occupies $\mathbf{P} \times 10^{-23} \mathrm{~m}^2$ surface area on charcoal, the value of $\mathbf{P}$ is _______ [Use given data: Surface area of charcoal $=1.5 \times 10^2 \mathrm{~m}^2 \mathrm{~g}^{-1} ;$ Avogadro's number $\left(\mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{A}}\right)=6.0 \times 10^{23}$ $\left.\mathrm{mol}^{-1}\right]$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text{ Millimole$ of $acid taken }=100 \times 0.5=50 \\ & \text{ Millimole of } \mathrm{NaOH} \text{ used }=40 \times 1=40 \\ & \text{ Millimole of acid adsorbed }=50-40=10 \\ & \text{ Molecules of acid adsorbed }=10 \times 10^{-3} \times 6 \times 10^{23}=6 \times 10^{21} \\ & \text{ Surface area occupied per molecule }=\frac{1.5 \times 10^2}{6 \times 10^{21}}=0.25 \times 10^{-19}=2500 \times 10^{-23}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
To check the principle of multiple proportions, a series of pure binary compounds $\left({P}_{m}{Q}_{n}\right)$ were analysed and their composition is tabulated below. The correct option(s) is(are)

Compound Weight $% of P$ Weight $% of Q$
$1$ $50$ $50$
$2$ $44 . 4$ $55 . 6$
$3$ $40$ $60$
options: If empirical formula of compound $3$ is ${P}_{3}{Q}_{4}$, then the empirical formula of compound $2$ is ${P}_{3}{Q}_{5}$.
If empirical formula of compound $3$ is ${P}_{3}{Q}_{2}$ and atomic weight of element $P$ is $20$ , then the atomic weight of $Q$ is $45 .$
If empirical formula of compound $2$ is $PQ$, then the empirical formula of the compound $1$ is ${P}_{5}{Q}_{4}$.
If atomic weight of $P$ and $Q$ are $70$ and $35$, respectively, then the empirical formula of compound $1$ is ${P}_{2}Q$.
questions.solution:
(A) If empirical formula of $3$ is ${P}_{3}{Q}_{4}$, then molecular formula is ${\left({P}_{3}{Q}_{4}\right)}_{n}$

$⇒ \dfrac{3{M}_{P}}{3{M}_{P} + 4{M}_{Q}} = \dfrac{40}{100} = \dfrac{2}{5}$

$15{M}_{p} = 6{M}_{p} + 8{M}_{Q}$

$9{M}_{P} = 8{M}_{Q}$

$∴$ For ${P}_{3}{Q}_{5}, %$ of $P = \left(\dfrac{3{M}_{P}}{3{M}_{P} + 5{M}_{Q}}\right) \times 100 = \dfrac{8{M}_{Q}}{23{M}_{Q}} \times 100 = 34 . 78 %$

(B) If empirical formula of compound $3$ is ${P}_{3}{Q}_{2}$, we have

$\dfrac{3{M}_{P}}{3{M}_{P} + 2{M}_{Q}} = \dfrac{2}{5}$

$15{M}_{P} = 6{M}_{P} + 4{M}_{Q}$

$9Mp = 4{M}_{Q}$

If ${M}_{p} = 20$

${M}_{Q} = \dfrac{180}{4} = 45$
(C) If empirical formula of $2$ is $PQ$

$∴ \dfrac{{M}_{P}}{{M}_{P} + {M}_{Q}} = \dfrac{4}{9} = \dfrac{44 . 44}{100}$

$9Mp = 5Mp + 4MQ$

$5{M}_{P} = 4{M}_{Q}$

If empirical formula is assumed as ${P}_{5}{Q}_{4}$,

$%$ of $P = \left(\dfrac{5{M}_{P}}{5{M}_{P} + 4{M}_{Q}}\right) \times 100 = 50$

Hence ${P}_{5}{Q}_{4}$ is the empirical formula of compound

(D) If empirical formula of $I$ is ${P}_{2}Q$, we have

$% ofP = \left(\dfrac{2{M}_{P}}{2{M}_{P} + {M}_{Q}}\right) \times 100 = 50$

$4{M}_{p} = 2{M}_{p} + {M}_{Q}$

$2{M}_{p} = {M}_{Q}$

Hence, atomic weight of $P$ and $Q$ cannot be $70$ and $35$ respectively.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The treatment of an aqueous solution of $3 . 74g$ of $Cu{\left({NO}_{3}\right)}_{2}$ with excess $KI$ results in a brown solution along with the formation of a precipitate. Passing ${H}_{2}S$ through this brown solution gives another precipitate $X$. The amount of $X$ (in $g$) is____[Given: Atomic mass of $H = 1, N = 14, O = 16, S = 32, K = 39, Cu = 63, I = 127$]
questions.solution:
Number of moles of $Cu{\left({NO}_{3}\right)}_{2} = \dfrac{3 . 74}{187} = 0 . 02$

$2Cu{\left({NO}_{3}\right)}_{2} + 4KI \to {Cu}_{2}{I}_{2} ↓ + {I}_{2} + 4{KNO}_{3}$

Number of moles of ${Cu}_{2}{l}_{2}$ precipitated $= 0 . 01$

${I}_{2}\left(brownsolution\right) + {H}_{2}S \to S ↓ + 2HI$

Number of moles of $S$ precipitated $= 0 . 01$

Mass of $S$ precipitates $= \left(0 . 01 \times 32\right)g = 0 . 32g$

Reaction of $\mathbf{x}$ g of $\mathrm{Sn}$ with $\mathrm{HCl}$ quantitatively produced a salt. Entire amount of the salt reacted with $\mathbf{y} g$ of nitrobenzene in the presence of required amount of $\mathrm{HCl}$ to produce $1.29 \mathrm{~g}$ of an organic salt (quantitatively).
(Use Molar masses (in $\mathrm{g} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ ) of $\mathrm{H}, \mathrm{C}, \mathrm{N}, \mathrm{O}, \mathrm{Cl}$ and $\mathrm{Sn}$ as $1,12,14,16,35$ and 119 , respectively).
The value of $x$ is _______ .
questions.solution:
Mass of salt produced $= 1 . 29g$

Moles of salt produced $= \dfrac{1 .29}{129} = 0 .01 mole$

To produce, $0 . 01mole$ organic salt $0 . 01mole$

${PhNO}_{2}$ and $0 . 03\text{mole}{SnCl}_{2}$ is required.

$0 . 03mole{SnCl}_{2}$ is produced from $0 . 03\text{mole}$ $Sn .$

Mass of $Sn = xgm = 0 .03 \times 119 = 3 .57 g$

Mass of ${PhNO}_{2} = ygm = 0 .01 \times 123 = 1 .23 g$

$x = 3 .57 y = 1 . 23$

questions.q: Aluminium reacts with sulfuric acid to form aluminium sulfate and hydrogen. What is the volume of hydrogen gas in liters $( L )$ produced at $300K$ and $1 . 0$ atm pressure, when $5 . 4g$ of aluminium and $50 . 0mL$ of $5 . 0M$ sulfuric acid are combined for the reaction? (Use molar mass of aluminium as $27 . 0g{mol}^{- 1}$, $R = 0 . 082atmL{mol}^{- 1}{K}^{- 1}$)
questions.solution:
$2AI + 3{H}_{2}{SO}_{4} ⟶ {AI}_{2}{\left({SO}_{4}\right)}_{3} + 3{H}_{2}$

$\dfrac{5 . 7}{27}$ $\dfrac{50 \times 5}{1000}$

$= 0 . 2mole$ $\mathop{= 0 .25 mole}_{( Limitingreagent )}$

$∴$ $0 .25 mole{\text{H}}_{2}$ is formed

$PV = nRT$

$V = \dfrac{nRT}{P} = \dfrac{0 . 25 \times 0 . 082 \times 300}{1atm}$

$= 6 . 15$ litre

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The mole fraction of urea in an aqueous urea solution containing $900g$ of water is $0.05$ . If the density of the solution is $1.2g{cm}^{- 3}$ , the molarity of urea solution is _______
(Given data: Molar masses of urea and water are $60g{mol}^{- 1}$ and $18g{mol}^{- 1}$ , respectively)
questions.solution:
Mole fraction $⇒ 0.05$
Number of moles of water $⇒ \dfrac{900}{18} = 50$
$∴ \dfrac{{n}_{urea}}{{n}_{urea} + 50} = 0.05$
${n}_{urea} = 2.63$
Mass of urea $= \left({W}_{urea}\right) = 2.63 \times 60 ⇒ 157.8g$
Total mass of solution $⇒ 157.8 + 900 ⇒ 1057.8g$
Volume of solution $⇒ \dfrac{1057.8}{1.2}ml ⇒ 881.5ml$
Molarity $⇒ \dfrac{no . ofmolesofsolutions}{volumeofsolutioninL} ⇒ \dfrac{2.63}{0.8815} ⇒ 2.98M$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Galena (an ore) is partially oxidized by passing air through it at high temperature. After some time, the passage of air is stopped, but the heating is continued in a closed furnace such that the contents undergo self-reduction. The weight (in $kg$) of $Pb$ produced per $kg$ of ${O}_{2}$ consumed is ____. (Atomic weights in $g{mol}^{- 1}: O = 16, S = 32, Pb = 207$)
questions.solution:
$molofPb = molof{O}_{2}$
$= \dfrac{1000}{32}mol$

$mass = moles \times molecularmass$
$∴$    Mass of $Pb = \dfrac{1000}{32} \times 207g$
$= \dfrac{207}{32}kg = 6 . 47kg$

$mass = moles \times molecularmass$

questions.q: The mole fraction of a solute in a solution is $0 . 1$. At $298K$, the molarity of this solution is the same as its molality. The density of this solution at $298K$ is $2.0gc{m}^{– 3}$. The ratio of the molecular weights of the solute and solvent, $\left(\dfrac{M{W}_{solute}}{M{W}_{solvent}}\right)$, is:
questions.solution:
$1$ mole solution has $0 . 1$ mole solute and $0 . 9$ mole solvent.
Let ${M}_{1} =$Molar mass of solute
${M}_{2} =$Molar mass of solvent
Molality, $m = \dfrac{0.1}{0.9{M}_{2}} \times 1000 \ldots . . \left(1\right)$
Molarity, $M = \dfrac{0.1}{0.1{M}_{1} + 0.9{M}_{2}} \times 2 \times 1000 \ldots . . \left(2\right)$
$∵ m = M$
$⇒ \dfrac{0.1 \times 1000}{0.9{M}_{2}} = \dfrac{200}{0.1{M}_{1} + 0.9{M}_{2}}$
$⇒ \dfrac{{M}_{1}}{{M}_{2}} = 9$

questions.q: $29.2 \%(\mathrm{w} / \mathrm{w}) \mathrm{HCl}$ stock solution has a density of $1.25 \mathrm{gmL}^{-1}$. The molecular weight of $\mathrm{HCl}$ is $36.5 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$. The volume $(\mathrm{mL})$ of stock solution required to prepare a 200 $\mathrm{mL}$ solution of $0.4 \mathrm{M} \mathrm{HCl}$ is :
questions.solution:
Molarity of stock solution of $\mathrm{HCl}$

$=\frac{29.2 \times 1000 \times 1.25}{100 \times 36.5}$

Let the volume of stock solution required $=V \mathrm{~mL}$

Thus, $V \times \frac{29.2 \times 1000 \times 1.25}{100 \times 36.5}=200 \times 0.4$ $\Rightarrow V=8 \mathrm{~mL}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Paragraph: Chemical reactions involve interaction of atoms and molecules. A large number of atoms/molecules (approximately $6.023 \times 10^{23}$ ) are present in a few grams of any chemical compound varying with their atomic/molecular masses. To handle such large numbers conveniently, the mole concept was introduced. This concept has implications in diverse areas such as analytical chemistry, biochemistry, electrochemistry and radiochemistry. The following example illustrates a typical case, involving chemical/electrochemical reaction, which requires a clear understanding of the mole concept. A $4.0$ molar aqueous solution of $\mathrm{NaCl}$ is prepared and $500 \mathrm{~mL}$ of this solution is electrolysed. This leads to the evolution of chlorine gas at one of electrodes (atomic mass: $\mathrm{Na}=23, \mathrm{Hg}=200 ; 1$ faraday $=96500$ coulombs).Question: The total number of moles of chlorine gas evolved is
questions.solution:
$4.0 \mathrm{M} \mathrm{NaCl} .500 \mathrm{~mL}(0.5 \mathrm{~L})$
Moles of $\mathrm{NaCl}=4 \times 0.5=2$
2 moles $\mathrm{NaCl} \equiv 2$ moles $\mathrm{Cl}^{-} $
\underset{2 $\text{ mole }$}{2 $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$} \longrightarrow $\mathrm{Cl}_2 $
